youtube_description:
⏱️ TIMELINE COMPARISON: The 2022 Crypto Crash Runaway (Chart Race)

00:00 — The 2021 peak: Bitcoin breaks toward the top of the market (BTC market cap ~ $1.0T) while Ethereum surges (~ $430B). Stablecoins balloon as traders park value.

00:20 — 2022 starts hot, but risk gets repriced: BTC slips from ~ $1.0T down to ~ $350B by year’s end. ETH falls harder, from ~ $430B to ~ $150B.

00:45 — The stablecoin shock (May–June 2022): UST reaches a peak market value around ~ $18B in 2021, then collapses to ~$0 in 2022 after the depeg—instantly removing one of crypto’s fastest “value rails.”

01:05 — The exchange domino: FTX’s token (FTT) had grown rapidly into 2021 (market cap proxy up to ~ $20B). After the 2022 collapse, it plunges to ~ $1B during the selloff, then effectively to $0 in later years.

01:30 — 2023–2024: The market rebuilds the “core”: BTC rebounds to ~ $750B (2023) and ~ $1.1T (2024). ETH follows with ~ $220B (2023) and ~ $500B (2024).

01:55 — 2025–2026: Liquidity keeps expanding: Tether supply climbs steadily (from ~ $60B in 2022 to ~ $120B in 2025, ~ $130B in 2026 estimate), while BTC and ETH continue compounding into the next cycle.

📌 Watch the chart race closely: the dramatic part isn’t just BTC dropping—it’s how fast “confidence proxies” (UST, FTT) get wiped, while stablecoin rails (USDT) keep growing.

✅ If you enjoyed this chart race, like + subscribe for more data-driven viral history.

Sources used for historical anchors: widely reported market cap ranges for BTC/ETH across 2019–2026, UST collapse scale from major market coverage (depeg and near-total wipeout in 2022), and Tether circulating supply milestones from public issuer reporting/market tracking.
instagram_caption:
🚀 The $1T Crypto Crash—then the comeback no one saw coming.

In early 2021, crypto felt unstoppable. Bitcoin surged to about $1.0T in market cap, while Ethereum roared through roughly $430B—two giants pulling the whole market forward. Even stablecoins were booming: Tether (USDT) climbed to around $62B as traders increasingly moved value on-chain instead of waiting on traditional routes.

Then 2022 hit like a breaker. Bitcoin’s market cap slid from ~$1.0T down to about $350B by the end of the year. Ethereum dropped harder, from ~$430B to roughly $150B. But the most violent moment wasn’t just “prices down”—it was trust evaporating in real time.

Watch the stablecoin rail: UST. Its market value peaked around ~$18B in the 2021 run-up… and then it basically collapsed to ~$0 in 2022 after the depeg. In the same era, the exchange ecosystem also imploded. FTX’s token (FTT) went from a 2021-era high around ~$20B down to about ~$1B during the 2022 fallout—and thereafter effectively to $0. Those two lines are the “panic wipeout” effect: when systems fail, the charts don’t drift—they fall off a cliff.

And while other lines were getting crushed, the liquidity rail kept getting thicker. Tether supply didn’t collapse—it kept growing from about ~$60B in 2022 to ~$110B in 2024 and ~$120B in 2025, reaching about ~$130B in 2026 (trend projection).

By 2024, the core assets were back: Bitcoin near ~$1.1T and Ethereum around ~$500B. The last segment (2025–2026) shows the pattern repeating—BTC to about ~$1.25T–$1.35T, ETH to ~$560B–$620B, supported by the growing stablecoin base.

Now your turn: In a future crash, which would you bet survives the longest—BTC, ETH, or the “liquidity rails” like USDT?
facebook_caption:
The 2022 crypto collapse didn’t move all assets the same way. Bitcoin fell from an approximate ~$1.0T peak in 2021 to ~$350B by end of 2022, while Ethereum declined from roughly ~$430B to about ~$150B. The sharpest destruction, however, came from failure of confidence-driven systems. UST (TerraUSD)—which had reached an estimated ~$18B market value in 2021—collapsed to effectively ~$0 during 2022 following the depeg event. Similarly, the FTX-linked token (FTT) peaked around ~$20B in 2021 and then dropped to ~ $1B during the 2022 breakdown, effectively fading to $0 afterward.

Meanwhile, “liquidity rails” kept expanding. Tether (USDT) circulation grew from about ~$60B in 2022 to ~$110B in 2024 and ~$120B in 2025, reaching an estimated ~$130B in 2026. The chart race illustrates the central storyline: when the market risk premium spikes, speculative value proxies can vanish quickly—while liquidity and core network assets recover over the following years.
